data.body:
J4 0a94 HELD-OUT VALIDATION -> GREEN. 27 tests: 13 happy-path (the only file the implementer saw) + 14 HELD OUT.
TIERING: standard/mid tier (sonnet), named explicitly on dispatch. Implementer reported 2 ATTEMPTS to green the happy path — its first port of Cloud's logic returned the LOCAL value on an authoritative-but-mismatched DC lookup, where DC must emit the resolved username (for DC the 'name' IS the identity, whereas Cloud only trusts the resolved value on its is_account_id fast-path). It fixed this by parameterizing the shared state machine with trust_resolved_on_mismatch rather than forking it. That is the correct shape and NOT an escalation trigger: it was a first held-out-style miss on a case the happy-path spec did pin, resolved within the same dispatch. Zero escalations across J2 and J4.
RESULT SHAPE: identity_model.py holds ONE shared _resolve state machine parameterized by (remote_key, force_is_account_id_false, trust_resolved_on_mismatch); AccountIdIdentity and NameIdentity are thin wrappers. The state machine exists once — the copy-paste PR #120 made is structurally absent.

MY OWN TEST DEFECT, FOUND AND FIXED DURING VALIDATION: 7 held-out parity tests failed with AttributeError: 'JiraBackend' object has no attribute 'resolve_assignee'. Investigated instead of assuming implementer fault — resolve_assignee lives on the _JiraOutbound ROLE (backend.py:98, reached as backend.outbound.resolve_assignee), not on the JiraBackend facade. My test used the wrong accessor. Fixed the TEST, not the code, and did NOT escalate a tier: the skill's escalation rule keys on held-out BEHAVIORAL tests going red against the implementation, and this red was my own wrong accessor path. RED-first integrity is intact — before the implementation the module did not exist at all, so the corrected test was RED for the right reason (ModuleNotFoundError) regardless of the accessor.

MUTATION / TEETH (3 perturbations, each reverted; ALL verified to actually apply):
 1. Inserted 'authoritative = False' after the resolver call — a faithful reproduction of PR #120's never-set-resolver dead branch => test_data_center_is_authoritative_for_a_resolvable_assignee FIRED with its intended message, plus the convergence test. This is the exact defect the story exists to prevent, and the oracle catches it.
 2. Swapped DC's remote_key from 'name' to 'account_id' => 4 tests RED across both files (converged, desired-unassigned, payload shape).
 3. Broke the CONVERGED branch to return the resolved value instead of None => the second-pass convergence test RED ('a converged assignee must emit nothing on the next pass').
 Restored => 27/27 green.
 PROCESS NOTE: my first attempt at mutation 1 was a silent NO-OP (a regex that matched nothing). I caught it because the script printed 'NO-OP (pattern absent)' and REDID it with an exact-anchor edit rather than banking the meaningless 14-passed result. A mutation that does not apply proves nothing.

CLOUD PARITY: the strongest held-out test evaluates BOTH sides live — AccountIdIdentity.resolve vs the real JiraBackend.outbound.resolve_assignee across all 7 documented states (empty, no-resolver, non-authoritative, converged, desired-unassigned, accountId fast-path, resolvable-mismatched, plus no-remote-identity). Asserting equality against the LIVE backend rather than copied literals means the two cannot silently drift.
PRE-FLIGHT: make lint GREEN, make typecheck GREEN (386 files), tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ 1534 passed. Full suite running.
